subject: literature
passage: For three evenings, Mrs. Nwosu worked on Adaeze's graduation dress at the small table by the window, letting out the seams and raising the hem by two careful centimeters. When Adaeze finally tried it on, she turned slowly in front of the mirror and could not stop smiling. Mrs. Nwosu only nodded, but later that night Adaeze heard her tell her sister on the phone ______ the dress was the finest thing she had sewn all year.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "That the dress was the finest thing she had sewn all year" is what Mrs. Nwosu told her sister, so it works as the object of the verb "tell." No punctuation belongs between a verb and its object, even when a short phrase such as "on the phone" comes between them.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause, and it can't come between a verb and its object.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma can't separate the verb "tell" from its object, the clause beginning with "that."
explanation.C: Correct. No punctuation separates the verb "tell" from the "that" clause that serves as its object.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but "that the dress was …" is not one; it is the object of "tell."
